context:
The trust field already flows through the manifest. This TODO is
entirely about rendering - no data pipeline changes. Build the badge
first as an isolated component (snapshot-tested), then drop it into
three places (QueryHeatmap, BenchmarkIndex list view, Compare header).

Filter chips use the same pattern as existing filter controls on
BenchmarkIndex; reuse that UI vocabulary so trust filtering looks
native rather than bolted on.
description:
The original strategy proposal suggested defaulting the leaderboard to
`trust: maintainer-run` and hiding community results unless explicitly
opted in. The 2026-04-15 adversarial review rejected this: hiding
community results by default **defeats the entire value of BenchBox's
trust model**. The right pattern is to show everything and render the
trust tier as a visible per-row badge, with trust as an optional filter.

This TODO:

1. Adds a Trust column to QueryHeatmap rows and the list-view fallback,
   rendered as a small colored badge (maintainer = green, community =
   blue, unknown/CI/local = neutral gray).

2. Adds a trust filter control to BenchmarkIndex that defaults to "All"
   (shows every tier) with chips for each tier a user can deselect.

3. Sorts rows by primary metric within the default "All" view, not by
   trust tier - the trust model is informational, not a sort key.

4. Propagates trust_label through to the Compare page header so trust
   disparities in a comparison are also visible there.

Explicitly rejected: defaulting to "maintainer-run only" or visually
de-emphasizing community results via reduced opacity. BenchBox's
differentiator is the explicit trust model - make it pop.

anti_patterns.instead: default to showing everything with visible tier labels
render whatever the manifest provides, fall back gracefully on unknown values
anti_patterns.why: the existing manifest values are the source of truth

anti_patterns.instead: trust is informational, not a sort key
anti_patterns.why: metric-based ranking is the leaderboard's core value

anti_patterns.dont: use opacity or gray-out to de-emphasize non-maintainer tiers
anti_patterns.why: that reads as 'don't trust this' rather than 'here's the tier'

preserves.behavior: Default view shows all trust tiers - never hide community results by default
Existing trust_label values in manifest.json - do not reshape the vocabulary
Trust tier does not affect row ordering within the leaderboard - ranking stays metric-based
